## Objective 1. A world map to gain an appreciation for where the most occurrences of COVID-19 confirmations and deaths are located.

>
The interactive map below provides a global overview of COVID‑19 severity by visualizing confirmed cases and deaths for each country. Countries are represented by circle markers positioned at their geographic centroids, with color‑coded categories based on statistical quartiles. Two independent layers; Confirmed Cases and Deaths, allow users to toggle between infection and mortality patterns. Interactive pop‑ups display country‑level totals with a click, while dynamic legends clarify the meaning of each color scale. Together, these features offer a clear, comparative representation of the pandemic’s global impact and facilitate exploration of regional differences of the virus.
>


```{r Objetive1, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(leaflet)

df_confirmed_global <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CSSEGISandData/COVID-19/master/csse_covid_19_data/csse_covid_19_time_series/time_series_covid19_confirmed_global.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
df_deaths_global <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CSSEGISandData/COVID-19/master/csse_covid_19_data/csse_covid_19_time_series/time_series_covid19_deaths_global.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# --- Confirmed data set transposing dates columns onto a single column---
confirmed_global_long <- gather(
  df_confirmed_global,
  key = date,
  value = confirmed,
  -Province.State,
  -Country.Region,
  -Lat,
  -Long
)

confirmed_global <- confirmed_global_long %>%
  filter(confirmed > 0) %>%
  rename(Country = Country.Region,
         Province = Province.State) %>%
  select(Country, Lat, Long, confirmed) %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  summarize(latitude = mean(Lat, na.rm = FALSE),
            longitude = mean(Long, na.rm = FALSE),
            confirmed = sum(confirmed, na.rm = FALSE))

# --- Deaths data set trasposing dates columns into a single column for later grouping in countries---
deaths_global_long <- gather(
  df_deaths_global,
  key = date,
  value = deaths,
  -Province.State,
  -Country.Region,
  -Lat,
  -Long
)

deaths_global <- deaths_global_long %>%
  filter(deaths > 0) %>%
  rename(Country = Country.Region,
         Province = Province.State) %>%
  select(Country, Lat, Long, deaths) %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  summarize(latitude = mean(Lat, na.rm = FALSE),
            longitude = mean(Long, na.rm = FALSE),
            deaths = sum(deaths, na.rm = FALSE))

# --- Join both data sets
combined_global <- left_join(confirmed_global, deaths_global, by = "Country")

combined_global <- combined_global %>%
  mutate(
    latitude_x  = as.numeric(latitude.x),
    latitude_y  = as.numeric(latitude.y),
    longitude_x = as.numeric(longitude.x),
    longitude_y = as.numeric(longitude.y),
    latitude    = rowMeans(cbind(latitude_x, latitude_y), na.rm = TRUE),
    longitude   = rowMeans(cbind(longitude_x, longitude_y), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

combined_plot <- combined_global %>%
  select(Country, latitude, longitude, confirmed, deaths)

# --- Categories to distribute confirmed and deaths into quartiles
combined_plot <- combined_plot %>%
  mutate(
    conf_cat = cut(
      confirmed,
      breaks = quantile(confirmed, probs = c(0, .25, .75, 1), na.rm = TRUE),
      include.lowest = TRUE,
      labels = c("Low", "Middle", "High")
    ),
    death_cat = cut(
      deaths,
      breaks = quantile(deaths, probs = c(0, .25, .75, 1), na.rm = TRUE),
      include.lowest = TRUE,
      labels = c("Low", "Middle", "High")
    )
  )

combined_plot <- combined_plot %>%
  mutate(
    conf_cat = as.character(conf_cat),
    death_cat = as.character(death_cat)
  )

combined_plot_clean <- combined_plot %>%
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude))

#After finding out deaths categories had NA values...
# Fix NA death categories, this solved the issue of non-showing colors by categories!
#Decided to keep death_cat rows with NA values, classifying them as "unknown"

combined_plot_clean$death_cat[is.na(combined_plot_clean$death_cat)] <- "Unknown"

# --- Palette functions ---
palette_conf <- colorFactor(
  palette = c("blue", "gray", "green"),
  domain  = combined_plot_clean$conf_cat
)

palette_death <- colorFactor(
  palette = c("red", "orange", "purple", "black"),
  domain  = combined_plot_clean$death_cat
)

# --- Build the interactive Map :))) with markers and legends---
global_map <- leaflet(combined_plot_clean) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  setView(lng = 0, lat = 20, zoom = 2) %>%
  
  # Confirmed layer
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude,
    lat = ~latitude,
    color = ~palette_conf(conf_cat),
    fillOpacity = 0.6,
    stroke = FALSE,
    label = ~Country,
    popup = ~paste0(
      "<b>", Country, "</b><br>",
      "Confirmed: ", confirmed, "<br>",
      "Deaths: ", deaths
    ),
    group = "Confirmed Cases"
  ) %>%
  
  # Deaths layer
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude,
    lat = ~latitude,
    color = ~palette_death(death_cat),
    fillOpacity = 0.6,
    stroke = FALSE,
    label = ~Country,
    popup = ~paste0(
      "<b>", Country, "</b><br>",
      "Confirmed: ", confirmed, "<br>",
      "Deaths: ", deaths
    ),
    group = "Deaths"
  ) %>%
  
  # Layer control
  addLayersControl(
    overlayGroups = c("Confirmed Cases", "Deaths"),
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  
  # Legend for confirmed
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    pal = palette_conf,
    values = ~conf_cat,
    title = "Confirmed Categories",
    group = "Confirmed Cases"
  ) %>%
  
  # Legend for deaths
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomleft",
    pal = palette_death,
    values = ~death_cat,
    title = "Death Categories",
    group = "Deaths"
  )

global_map

```
